2022_273_biographical_sketches_2022_2023.paragraph: Biographical sketches of newly hired Troy School District certificated staff, carried in the Board of Education agenda for the September 20, 2022 meeting and covering appointments for the 2022-2023 school year. Each entry lists the assignment and FTE, degrees and majors with dates conferred, the Michigan teaching certificate or professional license held, prior employment, and the employee's community of residence. Assignments run across TSD Preschool, the elementary buildings, Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith middle schools, Athens High School and International Academy East, concentrated in special education, early childhood, counseling and speech pathology; nearly all are 1.0 FTE, with Anne Race at .8 and Samuel Mulhern at .6.
2022_273_biographical_sketches_2022_2023.page:
**Purpose and format**
A roster of biographical sketches for staff newly hired into the Troy School District for 2022-2023, submitted with the September 20, 2022 Board of Education agenda. Every sketch follows the same template: name, FTE and assignment; Educational Background (degree, institution, city, major/minor, month and year); certificate or license held; Teaching Experience (employer, city, role, month-year span); and Resident Community.

**Preschool, early childhood and speech**
TSD Preschool draws the largest single group: Emily Friedman (1.0 Early Childhood Special Education), Lori Hicks, Megan McGarry, Madisyn Penz, Allison Selden and Colleen Nietzel (1.0 Early Childhood Educators), plus speech pathologists Katie Nelson and Kristina Slifco.

**Elementary assignments**
Alexa Harrison (1.0 ASD Teacher, Barnard) and Carrie Couretas (1.0 Kindergarten, Barnard); Stefani Urlaub (1.0 second grade, Troy Union); Hallie Vawter (1.0 Elementary Music, Barnard/Hamilton); Dana Santilli (1.0 Level IV, Martell) and Alison Keaser (1.0 third grade, Martell); Victoria Zarbaugh (1.0 second grade, Wass) and Jami Kazdan (1.0 MICI, Wass); Kailee Comes (1.0 second grade, Wattles); Elena Eastman (1.0 fifth grade, Leonard) and Amy Przygoda (1.0 third grade, Leonard); Elizabeth Groth (1.0 Teacher Consultant, Morse) and Holly Montgomery (1.0 Kindergarten, Morse); Meghan Coppen (1.0 Kindergarten, Hamilton); Elizabeth Motzenbecker (1.0 Level IV, Schroeder); Christopher Kelly (1.0 Physical Education, Wattles/Schroeder).

**Middle schools**
Michelle Fletcher (1.0 ASD Teacher), Dominique Burke and Michelle Pozzo (1.0 Counselors) and Samuel Mulhern (.6 ELA) at Boulan Park; Madisen Parker (1.0 English) at Larson; Alina Kirtland (1.0 Science) and Allison Berns (1.0 History) at Baker; Shannon Burt (1.0 English/ELD) at Baker/Smith; Anne Race (.8 Social Studies) split between Boulan Park and Larson.

**High school and International Academy East**
Athens High School adds Maren Fischer and Colleen Duffy (1.0 English), Kelsey Blazoff (1.0 Counselor), Kelsey Kroenung (1.0 Level IV), Kathleen Raines (1.0 Spanish/ELA) and Kristin Warholak (1.0 Physics). International Academy East adds Matthew Szalkowski (1.0 English/Social Studies) and InSeong Hwang (1.0 Science).

**Preparation and pipeline**
Oakland University, Michigan State University, Grand Valley State University and Central Michigan University supply most degrees; out-of-state credentials come from Xavier University (Cincinnati), Ashland University (Ohio), Bowling Green State University, Arizona State University, DePaul University, Point Park University (Pittsburgh), the University of Colorado Denver and Western Governors University. Many hires come from inside the district's own substitute pipeline: Edustaff/EDUStaff guest-teaching assignments in Troy buildings appear for Vawter, Comes, Eastman, Keaser, Montgomery, Penz, Nietzel, Mulhern, Race, Burt, Couretas, Coppen and Hwang, and Zarbaugh, Blazoff and Selden served as Troy long-term substitutes.

**Residency**
Resident communities listed include Troy (Harrison, Parker, Zarbaugh, Eastman, Duffy, Burt, Kirtland, Nietzel), Lake Orion, Macomb, Roseville, Huntington Woods, Oxford, Sylvan Lake, Livonia, Clawson, Rochester, Rochester Hills, Royal Oak, Ortonville, Ferndale, Commerce Township, Southfield (printed "Sothfield"), Bloomfield, Bloomfield Township, Bloomfield Hills, Oak Park, Grosse Pointe Park, Sterling Heights, Shelby Township, Oakland and Waterford.

2022_275_2_a_2022_troy_board_presentatio.paragraph: Draft external-audit presentation to the Troy School District Board of Education for the year ended June 30, 2022, delivered on the October 4, 2022 agenda. The auditors report an unmodified opinion on the 2022 financial statements and an unmodified opinion on the federal program audit with no findings or questioned costs, along with bond and sinking fund compliance, GASB 87 implementation and Uniform Budget Act compliance. General Fund revenue of $170,116,893 against expenditures of $172,507,660 and net other financing sources of $2,637,502 left fund balance at $32,980,837, or 19.12% of total expenditures and other uses.

**Engagement and opinions**
Board presentation for the year ended June 30, 2022. Key audit highlights: unmodified opinion on the 2022 financial statement audit; unmodified opinion on the 2022 federal program audit with no findings or questioned costs; bond and sinking fund compliance; GASB 87 implementation; Uniform Budget Act; ASBO Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting - 2021; non-recurring funding sources of revenue; federal ESSER; and federal child care grants.

**General Fund revenue and expenditures**
Revenue of $170,116,893 breaks out as state source $111,699,626 (66%), local $37,421,546 (22%), federal $10,869,663 (6%) and interdistrict source $10,126,058 (6%). A second view splits the same total into state portion of foundation allowance $82,298,118 (48%), other state and local $41,328,022 (24%), property taxes $35,621,090 (21%) and federal $10,869,663 (7%). Expenditures of $172,507,660 by object: salaries and employee benefits $140,831,012 (82%), purchased services $22,737,810 (13%), supplies $6,263,072 (4%) and other expenses $2,675,766 (1%). By function: direct instruction 66.17%, indirect instruction 13.92%, operations and maintenance 7.02%, school administration 5.38%, pupil transportation 2.06%, general administration and business services 1.92%, central services 1.85%, athletics 1.29%, debt service 0.28% and community services 0.11%, against an Oakland County average for direct instruction for FY21 of 60.47%.

**Membership, foundation allowance and fund balance**
Membership and foundation allowance are charted for 2008-2009 (final year of 20j funding at $248.18 per pupil) and 2017-2018 through 2022-2023, with counts of 13,081, 13,096, 13,111, 13,070, 12,508, 12,429 and 12,177 (certain years noted as including preschool pupils) and allowances of $9,275, $9,075, $9,195, $9,315, $9,315, $9,430 and $9,870, under a "Super Blend" count. Among Oakland County districts in 2021-2022, Troy's $9,430 sits above Huron Valley, Waterford and Rochester at $8,700, Walled Lake $8,782, Novi $8,948, Royal Oak $9,231 and West Bloomfield $9,269, and below Farmington $10,533, Lamphere $10,922, Southfield $11,471, Birmingham $12,436 and Bloomfield Hills $12,517. Ten-year General Fund balance runs from $22,070,236 (FY2013, 16.76%) to $32,980,837 (FY2022, 19.12%), equal to 9.9 weeks or 70 days of operations.

**Outlook**
Public education funding for 2022-2023: Revenue Estimating Conference in January 2023, state foundation allowance funding gap eliminated, School Aid Fund stability with continued uncertainty, and MPSERS challenges. Budgeting themes are strategic utilization of one-time federal and state funding, monitoring of pupil counts, and a continued dynamic environment.
2022_275_2_a_2022_troy_board_presentatio.verbose:
Draft slide deck titled "2022 Troy Board presentation," presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on the October 4, 2022 agenda and covering the external audit for the year ended June 30, 2022.

**Key 2022 audit highlights**
The auditors list: 2022 Financial Statement Audit Results - Unmodified Opinion; 2022 Federal Program Audit Results - Unmodified Opinion with no findings or questioned costs; Bond and Sinking Fund Compliance; GASB 87 Implementation; Uniform Budget Act; ASBO Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting - 2021; Non-recurring funding sources of revenue; Federal ESSER; and Federal Child Care Grants.

**Non-recurring COVID-19 relief funding, awards and expenditures as of June 30, 2022**
Figures are stated in thousands. Total Allocated = $27,757 and Total Expended = $19,028. By award: CRF allocated $6,501 and expended $6,501; ESSER I allocated $246 and expended $246; ESSER II allocated $1,074 and expended $970; ESSER II Equal (State) allocated $5,036 and expended $5,036; ESSER III allocated $1,895 and expended $1,895; ESSER III Equal -11t allocated $12,385 and expended $3,760; GEER allocated $22 and expended $22; and ARP - IDEA allocated $598 and expended $598. The chart axis runs from $- to $12,000. The largest remaining unspent balance sits in the ESSER III Equal award, where expenditures trail the allocation substantially.

**Governmental funds revenue and expenditures, June 30, 2022**
Three columns are presented: General Fund, 2019 Capital Projects Fund, and Total Nonmajor Funds. Revenue: $170,116,893, $23,498 and $40,854,075. Expenditures: 172,507,660, 11,414,598 and 36,192,820. Excess of Revenue (Under) Over Expenditures: (2,390,767), (11,391,100) and 4,661,255. Other financing sources and uses comprise Transfers In of 1,200,000 in the General Fund and 8,411 in nonmajor funds; Transfers Out of (1,208,411) in nonmajor funds; Leases entered into of 492,818 in nonmajor funds; and Proceeds From Sale of Capital Assets of 1,437,502 in the General Fund. Total Other Financing Sources (Uses): 2,637,502, nil, and (707,182). Net Change in Fund Balances: 246,735, (11,391,100) and 3,954,073. Fund Balances - Beginning of Year: 32,734,102, 18,231,222 and 6,879,054. Fund Balances - End of Year: $32,980,837, $6,840,122 and $10,833,127. The 2019 Capital Projects Fund spent far more than it took in during the year, drawing down its bond proceeds.

**General Fund revenue**
Total General Fund revenue for June 30, 2022 is $170,116,893. The revenue-source pie shows state source revenue of $111,699,626 at 66%, local revenue of $37,421,546 at 22%, federal revenue of $10,869,663 at 6%, and interdistrict source revenue of $10,126,058 at 6%. A companion "Foundation" view of the same $170,116,893 total shows the State Portion of Foundation Allowance at $82,298,118 (48%), Other State and Local at $41,328,022 (24%), Property Taxes at $35,621,090 (21%), and Federal at $10,869,663 (7%).

**General Fund expenditures by object**
Total expenditures of $172,507,660 for June 30, 2022 divide into Salaries and Employee Benefits of 140,831,012 (82%), Purchased Services of 22,737,810 (13%), Supplies of 6,263,072 (4%) and Other Expenses of 2,675,766 (1%).

**General Fund expenditures by function**
Against the same $172,507,660 total: Direct Instruction 66.17%; Indirect Instruction 13.92%; Operations and Maintenance 7.02%; School Administration 5.38%; Pupil Transportation 2.06%; General Administration and Business Services 1.92%; Central Services 1.85%; Athletics 1.29%; Debt Service 0.28%; and Community Services 0.11%. A footnote records that the Oakland County Average for Direct Instruction for FY21 was 60.47%, placing Troy well above the county norm on direct instruction.

**Per pupil membership and foundation allowance**
The chart covers 2008-2009, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023. Student population figures printed are 13,081; 13,096; 13,111; 13,070; 12,508; 12,429; and 12,177, with asterisked notes that 2008-2009 was the final year of 20j funding at $248.18 per pupil and that certain later years include preschool pupils. Foundation allowance figures printed are $9,275, $9,075, $9,195, $9,315, $9,315, $9,430 and $9,870; the district's blended count methodology is labeled "Super Blend." Chart gridlines are set at 5,000, 8,000, 11,000 and 14,000. Enrollment declines across the later years while the foundation allowance rises.

**Comparison of foundation revenue per pupil, Oakland County school districts 2021-2022**
Huron Valley $8,700; Waterford $8,700; Rochester $8,700; Walled Lake $8,782; Novi $8,948; Royal Oak $9,231; West Bloomfield $9,269; Troy $9,430; Farmington $10,533; Lamphere $10,922; Southfield $11,471; Birmingham $12,436; Bloomfield Hills $12,517. The scale runs from $- to $15,000. Troy sits in the middle of the county range, below the historically higher-funded hold-harmless districts.

**General Fund fund balance, last ten years ending June 30, 2022**
Balances and fund balance as a percentage of expenditures: FY2013 $22,070,236 at 16.76%; FY2014 $21,380,015 at 16.06%; FY2015 $20,701,637 at 15.08%; FY2016 $21,532,285 at 15.35%; FY2017 $24,205,391 at 16.86%; FY2018 25,242,472 at 16.75%; FY2019 $25,406,493 at 16.53%; FY2020 $26,009,710 at 16.58%; FY2021 $32,734,102 at 19.88%; and FY2022 $32,980,837 at 19.12%. The chart scale runs from 0 to 35,000,000.

**Changes in General Fund fund balance, year ended June 30, 2022**
Fund Balance - July 1, 2021 of 32,734,102; Revenue 170,116,893; Expenditures -172,507,660; Other financing sources (uses) - Net 2,637,502; Current Year Increase 246,735; and closing balance of 32,980,837 (the slide labels this line "Fund Balance - June 30, 2021" as printed). Fund balance as a percentage of total expenditures and other uses is 19.12%, equivalent to 9.9 weeks of operations or 70 days of operations.

**Public education funding 2022-2023**
Under K-12 funding the deck flags the Revenue Estimating Conference of January 2023, elimination of the state foundation allowance funding gap, stability in the School Aid Fund with remaining uncertainty, and MPSERS challenges. Under budgeting it flags strategic utilization of one-time federal and state funding, monitoring of pupil counts, and a continued dynamic environment. The deck closes with a thank-you slide.
